questions.question: Signals on a motorcycle:

options.text: Are more important than signals on larger vehicles.
Should not be used unless another vehicle is right next to the motorcycle.
Are less important than signals on larger vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are more important than signals on larger vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists are more at risk than car and truck drivers. Using signals is even more important for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: It is a good idea to drag your feet.
Your toes should be pointed downward.
You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
You should try to keep your feet away from the controls.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
questions.explanation: Keep your feet firmly on the footrests for proper balance. Do not drag your feet or point your toes down, as they may catch on the road. Keep your feet near the controls so you can reach them quickly if needed.

questions.question: To effectively provide protection for a motorcycle rider, pants should:

options.text: Be made of a soft material.
Be made of a heavy material.
Fit loosely enough that they flap in the wind.
Be short and expose some parts of the legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be made of a heavy material.
questions.explanation: Wear pants made of leather or another sturdy material that cover your entire legs. The pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind, but not so tight that they limit your movement.

questions.question: Since most crashes happen during daylight hours, you should:

options.text: Wear bright clothing all the time.
Ride on the shoulder and stay out of traffic.
Wear dark clothing all the time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing all the time.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during daylight. Always wear bright clothing when riding so other drivers can see you, even during the day.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may ride on the shoulder.
You may complete the pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and complete the pass within a passing zone.
You should sound your horn to get the other driver to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and complete the pass within a passing zone.
questions.explanation: All passing must happen in areas where passing is safe and legal. You must both start and finish the pass in a designated passing zone.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle:

options.text: Don't worry about checking the tire pressure.
Expect it to handle the same as your own bike.
The lender will make sure the brakes work so you don't have to.
Give yourself extra space when riding to allow more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give yourself extra space when riding to allow more time to react.
questions.explanation: Do all the same safety checks on a borrowed motorcycle as you would on your own bike. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar motorcycle and allow extra space when stopping.

questions.question: A danger of riding next to parked cars is:

options.text: You may not find a parking spot.
A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
Others may be driving slowly while looking for a parking spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver may suddenly pull out into your path.
questions.explanation: Riding next to parked cars is dangerous. A driver might suddenly pull out of a parking space into your path without looking. Car doors may open into your lane, and people may step out from between cars.

questions.question: ____ can remove alcohol and its effects from your body.
questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Only time can reduce your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers may keep you awake, but they cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: Most crashes occur in broad daylight. To be more visible, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wear bright clothing.
questions.explanation: Since most crashes happen in broad daylight, always wear bright clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle operator should be prepared for:

options.text: A driver to suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
Other drivers to see the motorcycle and stay out of its way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver to suddenly pull out of a parking space into traffic.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, be prepared for a car to suddenly pull out into traffic. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This gives you the most space between your motorcycle and any hazards.

questions.question: Low-speed crashes:

options.text: Happen frequently, so there is no need to worry about them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can be fatal.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even slow crashes can kill you.

questions.question: When approaching an uneven surface like a bump or pothole, rise slightly off your seat:

options.text: So you can jump off the motorcycle if needed.
So your legs can absorb the shock.
So other drivers can see you better.
So you can see the uneven surface better.

questions.correctAnswerText: So your legs can absorb the shock.
questions.explanation: Rising off your seat lets your joints absorb some of the impact force. This prevents the bump from throwing you off the motorcycle.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects you from:
questions.correctAnswerText: Insects.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your face from wind, dust, dirt, rain, insects, and rocks kicked up by other vehicles.

questions.question: Your body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone had eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks likely remain in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the hours passed from the drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining.

questions.question: Crashes are more likely to happen with:

options.text: Those who completed a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: New riders who are untrained and unfamiliar with their motorcycle crash more often.

questions.question: If you feel tired while riding, you should:

options.text: Keep going and hope you wake up.
Get off the road and rest.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get off the road and rest.
questions.explanation: Do not ride when tired. On long trips, take a rest break at least every two hours to avoid fatigue.

questions.question: If another driver is tailgating you, the best thing to do is:

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to get them in front of you. Change lanes safely and let them pass. Speeding up will only make them tailgate faster.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: Someone with a different type of motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can improve visibility by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Wearing bright clothing.
questions.explanation: To be seen by other drivers, wear bright clothing with reflective materials. Also use your headlight at all times and use your signals and brake light properly.

questions.question: You should do a pre-ride inspection:
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle is more dangerous than on a car. Inspect your motorcycle before every ride to stay safe.

questions.question: You should check your tires for all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Flexibility.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear. You do not need to check flexibility.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like food and drinks. This means:

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the drinker.
questions.explanation: Because it does not need to be digested, alcohol enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain within minutes. The body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: Passengers should:

options.text: Sit as far back on the bike as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when the operator leans.
questions.explanation: Passengers should sit directly behind the operator and lean as the operator leans. Sit as far forward as you can without crowding the operator, and hold onto the operator's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, the operator should:

options.text: Keep a longer distance between vehicles.
Let air out of the tires to handle the extra weight.
Not warn passengers of hazards ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a longer distance between vehicles.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger. The operator should stay farther away from other vehicles to have more time to react.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.
